source.title: Hidden Synergy: L1 Weight Normalization and 1-Path-Norm Regularization

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training cross-entropy for deep networks trained under several normalization and regularization conditions, bearing on whether overparameterized networks fit the training set; the benchmark and training recipe differ from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper’s Fashion-MNIST ablation reports training cross-entropy by model, including a standard residual network comparator. Tabular test-set performance, near-sparsity and pruning results do not measure the claim versions’ training-classification-error outcome and are not rows. Prior-work statements about other studies are not this paper’s results.
record.test_reason: The study uses identity shortcuts and orthogonal initialization in evaluating its proposed architectures and regularizers, but tests none of V1–V6. Table 3 measures training cross-entropy in fully connected Fashion-MNIST networks, without training classification error or the intervention comparisons required by the versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that weight normalization makes optimization with 1-path-norm regularization feasible in their overparameterized networks, and that their improved bound improves generalization. They describe good training fits except for the projected-gradient variant, and emphasize near-sparsity, pruning and reduced computation rather than establishing any of V1–V6.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies L1 weight normalization and 1-path-norm regularization on Fashion-MNIST and tabular data, rather than the claim versions’ specified benchmark and intervention comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported Fashion-MNIST training cross-entropy varies across normalization and regularizer choices; the authors say L1-normalized models converged slightly more slowly than L2-normalized models and that Pj-ResNet had optimization difficulties.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3 reports training cross-entropy from 0.083 to 0.315 across seven fixed-depth, fixed-width, fully connected Fashion-MNIST residual networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-normalized, overparameterized CReLU residual networks can achieve low training cross-entropy under several capacity-control recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report slightly slower convergence for L1 than L2 weight normalization and optimization difficulties for the projected-gradient variant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-normalization and projection choices affect convergence under a fixed optimization-step budget.

record.problems: Training cross-entropy is reported rather than training classification error; no uncertainty estimates are supplied for Table 3. The deep-network experiment uses one dataset and one fixed depth and width, and does not compare shortcut and plain networks.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Tabular test metrics and pruning/near-sparsity measurements do not measure a versioned training-classification-error result.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and dependence on model size, stopping or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, matched plain-versus-shortcut comparisons, and the special-initialization and normalization-free exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched initialization on training speed or trainable depth, including orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons. Shared orthogonal initialization does not test these effects.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All seven numerical training-loss values match Table 3. These are method-performance and ablation results that should remain contextual findings rather than evidence rows for the supplied versions. Section 4.2's statement that different initializations did not meaningfully change results concerns validation performance, without identified initialization conditions or training-speed/depth measurements; it does not challenge V4.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10/100, random-label, model-size or early-stopping comparison; Fashion-MNIST results do not test this version’s specified benchmarks or conditions.
No teacher-student two-layer ReLU experiment or width sweep against teacher size.
The ablation uses residual networks but does not compare plain networks with shortcut networks across depth, or test the specified ImageNet/CIFAR-10 claim.
Orthogonal initialization is used for all reported ablation models, without an initialization comparison or plain-network depth sweep.
No learning-rate stability threshold, loss-rise/curvature analysis, or sharpness tracking is reported.
No batch-normalization comparison or BN speed/high-learning-rate measurement; the ablation compares weight normalization and regularizers.
